propositions: Per-pair overlap judging issues 2N LLM calls for N candidates, re-sending the 846-token system prefix on each call; batching candidate verdicts into one call per ordering reduces this to 2*ceil(N/batch) calls, removing ~8,460 redundant prefix tokens for N=6.

The hoisted query digest in the system prompt reaches only 873 tokens, below the 1024-token model cache floor, producing zero cache hits; adding a batch protocol description in the system prompt lifts the prefix to 1,337 tokens and enables write-then-read caching.

Batching multiple candidates in one user message risks cross-contamination of verdicts; empirical measurement on a pinned query and six candidates shows identical surfaced findings (zero on both builds) and reproducible but mostly-conservative relation label shifts (5/6 divergences move away from surfacing), with a positive control recovering the true duplicate at full confidence.

The batched build achieves 9,116 input tokens versus 17,558 pre-8415 baseline (48.1% reduction) and 18,494 with 8415 alone (50.7% reduction), writing one prefix then reading it on the second call per ordering.

Demultiplexing must match verdicts by candidate_id label rather than response position to avoid cross-contamination; absent or malformed entries must abstain only the affected candidate, leaving others' verdicts intact.
The change is fail-safe: a raising runner or malformed batch response yields an empty verdict list with no exception propagating.
